Features: Given to Xbox Launch Team; says "Great work!" and has Bill Gates' signature on the jewel, as well as "Special Edition" on the front. Estimated 1000-2000 made. ^[2]
Released in Canada as a bundle with Fable and Crimson Skies. 100,000-150,000 consoles made, covering all available regions. ^[2]
Released in Japan.
Released as a second anniversary for the European release of the console.
Further UK releases.
"Limited Edition" written on jewel. Found in Australian / New Zealand crystal packs. Likely due to the jewel being sourced by multiple different suppliers, one of which may have added this text. ^[2]

Given to Electronic Arts for helping support Xbox Live. EA logo and "Special Edition" printed on front in blue and a black jewel with "Xbox Live" logo. Comes with two controllers, one with a red EA Sports jewel, and the other with a blue EA Games jewel. Reportedly, 110 made. ^[2] ^3

Says "Ed Fries - Special Edition" under Xbox logo on white jewel, and "Thanks for all you have done with MGS and Xbox" in red lettering on bottom right of the top. No stickers on bottom. Given to Ed Fries, the vice president of game publishing at Xbox at the time. One made.

Edition: Dead or Alive Ultimate / Kasumi-chan Blue (JP)
Features: Says "Dead or Alive Ultimate" on the bottom-left side of top and has a silver jewel. 5000 ^1 or 6000 ^1 made. They have a September 2004 manufacture date, but are actually 1.0 consoles with 2001 hardware and serial numbers.

Says "Dead or Alive Online" on the top, silver jewel. This was the original version that was meant to be sold before the game was renamed to "Dead or Alive Ultimate". One known to exist, previously owned by the international manager for the original Xbox launch, Stan Kaplita.
Released as a Halo bundle, says "Halo" on the front. 200,000 made, covering all regions.

First released on April 22nd, 2004; this NTSC console was made to commemorate the release of Xbox Live by Microsoft Hong Kong and Hong Kong Broadband Network Limited (HKBN). Four digit serial number on top indicates less than 10,000 units produced. ^3
Released in Southeast Asia; has a Halo 2 decal sticker on the top of the console near the disc drive. Number produced is unknown. ^3
Released as a Halo 2 bundle (no headset) in Canada, silver jewel.
Released as Halo 2 bundle in Asia, black jewel.

Given as a scratchcard prize in UK theaters to commemorate the release of the Hulk movie and possibly more given away in a contest ^3 . Has the Hulk's eye and Pepsi logo in the jewel. Estimated 36 given away, up to 50 made. ^[2]
Sold through a Mountain Dew sweepstakes ^3 . Mountain Dew logo on jewel. 1000 ^[2] to 5099 ^? made.
"MSN" and butterfly logo on front right. Likely made as a mock up for a potential MSN ISP promotion ^[2]. One known to exist, found in Denmark.
Colorful "MSN" and butterfly logo on front right. Likely made as a mock up for a potential MSN ISP promotion ^[2]. Two known to exist, found in Denmark.
Screenprinted artwork and logo surrounding jewel. 999 originally planned to be sold ^3 . 3,000 made, 1,300 shipped ^[2] .
Given to hardware companies involved with Xbox. Has "Thanks for Partnering with Xbox" and Bill Gates' signature on the jewel. Estimated 100 ^[2] or 1000 ^? made.

Released in Japan for the 2004 anniversary with a silver jewel saying "Limited Edition 2004". The unit number out of 1000 is engraved in the bottom left of the top side as well as an optional engraved name of up to 20 letters. 1000 made. They have a 2004 manufacture date, but are actually 1.0 Xboxes.

Internally referred to as "dark crystal", also called "smoke" or "skeleton". Release version in Japan that came with serialized key chain with a number from 1 to 50,000. 50,000 produced, estimated 10,000 sold on launch week. [1]

50 given away in The Chronicles of Riddick DVD sweepstakes ^3 , given away by a traveling Holiday Game Squad ^3 , or with purchase of 12-month Bell Canada's 'Sympatico High-Speed' contract ^3 . Came in box with Halo 2 and a headset, unlike the Canadian Halo 2 edition.
Sold in Canada.
Released for one year anniversary for the European release of the console. 20,000 manufactured. 5,000 sold.
Color mock up consoles. Two known to still exist, gifted to an internal marketing employee and a friend which was later stolen from their house. ^[2]
Color test prototypes. "Halo" written on front, one has a silver jewel, possibly added later on, and one has a black jewel. Three known to exist. ^2 ^3
Opaque candy apple / fire engine red (sample on table), glow in the dark, burgundy/dark magenta crystal, metallic gold, and a unit filled with color shifting beads. All likely destroyed. ^[2]
Given away by Australian television channel Channel V. Has "50 Cent Bulletproof" written in gold on top near the middle, and 50 Cent's signature. One made.

One given away in Australia, and one in New Zealand. Has "50 Cent Bulletproof" written in gold on top in the bottom left, black swirl designs on it, and 50 Cent's signature. Four made by Advanced Airbrush, all slightly different.[2]
Larger "50 Cent Bulletproof" written in gold on the top in the bottom left, 50 Cent's face airbrushed in the top right, and 50 Cent's signature. One made.
A black Xbox painted orange with an Atari logo on the jewel, and "Atari" written on top. Given away at the Leipzig Game Convention in 2004. Five made.
Has an image of Conker on top, with camouflage prints, bullet holes, and "Conker" written on it. Three made for a Conker's tournament in Sydney, Australia.

Edition: Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball
Features: Has a full volleyball beach scene airbrushed on top. 20 sold in Germany.
Had an image of Master Chief with the sky and Halo ring in the background to celebrate Halo's launch in the UK. Given out in one case by Microsoft employees at training event competitions. 5-10 made.
Commissioned by Microsoft to have an airbrushed top shell, these could be won from Media Markt for the Halo 2 launch. Painted by Peter Tronser. 100 made. ^3

Sold in a unique box with an undefined Samsung TV from Best Denki in Singapore. Has pink Hello Kitty Mission Rescue artwork painted on top. Came with a crystal controller with a unique gold and silver sparkle in the jewel. 550 made. ^3
Has sticker artwork on top of Penelope Juarez and a written letter, as well as artwork on the front. One unit made and given away in Australia in an unknown contest. ^3
Painting sanctioned by game publisher. Given away to winners of skateboarding competitions. Graffiti-style art on top on of crystal edition Xbox. Possible matching skateboard deck. 10 made.
Used for developing Xbox games. Large aluminum desktop tower.
Used for developing Xbox games. Large aluminum desktop tower.

"Debug Kit" written on bottom stickers. Often times "Debug Kit" written on front, though not always the case. Also may or may not have "Dolby Digital" and "Compact Disc" logos etched above the fourth controller port.
Used by game developers to hide the fact that games are running on a debug kit at trade shows.

Used for developing Xbox games. "Development Kit" written in green on front, and early to mid-production units have a green jewel with metallic lettering and later ones had a dark green jewel with standard lettering. USB port exposed on the back. On the bottom, it is referred to as a "BETA" and prototype system.

Used for developing Xbox games. "Development Kit" written in green on front. USB port exists but is blocked by the casing on the back. On the bottom, it is referred to as a "FINAL" and prototype system.
Used for developing Xbox games. "Development Kit" written in green on the front. Two known to exist, but an advertisement seems to show a third one. One was shown in a NVIDIA Twitter post.[3]
A giant X-shaped unit with developer hardware inside for the Xbox reveal at GDC 2000 by Bill Gates and various other showings. Two functional units made, with extra spare parts.
Microsoft TechNet logo on top of console, boots to XDK dashboard. PAL only. One known to exist. ^3
Used internally at Microsoft to test new system configurations. 3
Looks identical to a retail console with stickers. Sticker with "QT DVT2". Appears to be for testing the speed of some function.

Looks identical to a retail console with stickers. Sticker on the front labelled (XB DVT2) with a config and test ID and appears to have a unique 4604.1 BETA live kernel used internally at Microsoft to test Xbox Live. ^3
Pre-release Xbox. Some are known to have CPUs clocked at 750MHz rather than 733MHz.
Pre-release Xbox. Has a ribbon cable running from the LPC header, through the vent grille, and out the back. Likely used to flash and test new kernels.

"Prototype" and "LIVE ENABLED" written on bottom stickers, otherwise identical to retail unit. Only one known, claimed to be a DVT6 and internally called "Xbox console Xmode3 w/genealogy" by owner. ^3
Made a month before release, a final build prototype.

"Debug Kit" written on bottom stickers. "Debug Kit" written on front, covered by a BETA sticker, and "LIVE ENABLED" stickers on bottom. Also comes with a Xbox Live beta tester kit including an orange memory card.
"Debug Kit" written on bottom stickers. "Debug Kit" written on front, covered by a BETA sticker. Also comes with a Xbox Live beta tester kit including an orange memory card.
